reconcile.connective: Defenders harmonize by reading Stephen's clause as a compressed double reference — Abraham's Machpelah purchase telescoped together with Jacob's separate Shechem purchase.

discrepancy.connective: The objection these very commentators are answering was pressed by Isaac of Troki, who charged that Stephen wrongly assigns to Abraham a purchase from the sons of Hamor that Genesis attributes to Jacob.

skeptic.name: Isaac ben Abraham of Troki
skeptic.attribution: Isaac ben Abraham of Troki (d. 1594), Chizzuk Emunah (Faith Strengthened), pt. 2, ch. 63 (c. 1593)

excerpts.excerpt_text: …what best seems to remove the difficulty is, that the words refer to both places and purchases; to the field of Machpelah bought by Abraham, and to the parcel of field is Sichem bought by Jacob, of the sons of Emmor …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly addresses the Abraham-vs-Jacob / Machpelah-vs-Shechem purchase conflict by proposing that Stephen's clause is a compressed double reference covering both transactions — the strongest single harmonization on the row.

pd_work.resource: John Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John Haley
pd_work.note: Haley treats Acts 7:16 directly, arguing Stephen contracted two distinct sepulchres, places, and purchases into one summarizing clause.
